evals.prompt: /ci-generate github — this is a Node/TypeScript project with no CI yet, set one up
assertions: Explores the project (package.json scripts, lockfile) before writing any workflow, instead of assuming commands
Generates .github/workflows/ci.yml using the exact lint/test/build scripts found in package.json, not invented ones
Pins action versions to specific tags rather than using 'latest'
Includes lint, test, and build stages, with security/dependency scanning included by default
Validates the generated YAML (e.g. via python3 yaml.safe_load) and presents a summary of stages and required secrets
The summary does not include a fabricated estimated run time per stage

evals.prompt: We already have a .gitlab-ci.yml, can you add a deploy stage to Docker for it?
assertions: Reads the existing .gitlab-ci.yml before making any changes
Asks whether to replace or augment the existing config, or otherwise clearly preserves the user's existing custom stages
Adds a Docker-targeted deploy stage using GitLab CI syntax (not GitHub Actions or CircleCI syntax)
Cross-references that referenced commands/paths/images actually exist in the project before finalizing

evals.prompt: /ci-generate github --deploy aws --monorepo for our Python monorepo (api/ and worker/ services)
assertions: Detects Python tooling/version and per-service structure before generating the pipeline (Phase 1 discovery)
Produces a matrix or path-filtered workflow structure reflecting the --monorepo flag
Includes an AWS-specific deployment stage distinct from generic deploy boilerplate
Lists required secrets/environment variables for the AWS deploy in the final summary
Does not include services (e.g. Redis, Postgres) unless they are confirmed project dependencies

The deploy step references the image tag/digest produced by the build job (e.g. via job outputs consumed in a task-definition render or equivalent) rather than issuing a blind restart like 'aws ecs update-service --force-new-deployment' with no image reference

evals.prompt: add a deploy stage to our CI pipeline (no platform argument given, no existing deploy config, no hosting service referenced anywhere in the project's dependencies or config files)
assertions: Does not silently pick a deployment platform (e.g. Vercel, AWS, Netlify) when none is specified and none is inferable from project config
Asks the user which deployment target to use before generating or writing any deploy stage
Does not write, create, or modify any CI config file before the user answers the clarifying question
No deploy-related command (docker push, vercel deploy, aws ecs, etc.) appears anywhere in the run's output
The run's final message ends on the clarifying question about deployment target rather than proceeding with a guessed pipeline
